💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mikel Arteta may prefer to imagine his Arsenal team as a remorseless winning machine, although on nights such as these they can still demonstrate a familiar unreliability when it comes to the main purpose of it all.
  • There were 30 shots over the night from the English champions, only four of which were on target, and in the end their winner never came.
  • Industry observers note that the leaders of the Bundesliga were traumatised at times by the ferocity of the Arsenal press, and there were times when Borussia Dortmund will likely have no idea how they survived.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mikel Arteta may prefer to imagine his Arsenal team as a remorseless winning machine, although on nights such as these they can still demonstrate a familiar unreliability when it comes to the main purpose of it all.

There were 30 shots over the night from the English champions, only four of which were on target, and in the end their winner never came. Even in the 95th minute, Arteta’s players were still conspiring to foul it up. This Champions League game might have been decided in Arsenal’s favour within 20 minutes. By half-time it should have been a formality. Yet, as chance after chance slipped away, there was always a possibility this would end differently.

Industry observers note that the leaders of the Bundesliga were traumatised at times by the ferocity of the Arsenal press, and there were times when Borussia Dortmund will likely have no idea how they survived. Even so, they did just that and, liberated in the second half, Maximilian Beier scored an improbable equaliser in his team’s best period. There were still 40 minutes for Arsenal to put this one to bed and they found many ways not to do so.

It was notable that the man who put Arsenal ahead in the ninth minute with a right-foot thump from space on the edge of the Dortmund box was the same striker who would miss the best chance to win it. That is the Viktor Gyokeres dilemma. In the space of a single game he can look like a potential match-winner and also the last man his manager would wish to see arriving on the end of a perfect Martin Odegaard cross.

Industry observers note that so it proved on 75 minutes when Gyokeres thrust himself at an Odegaard ball into the box that just needed guiding inside the post, yet planted it decisively wide of the mark. On the touchline Arteta tried very hard to hide his despair and failed to do so.

It ended that way, with a heroic defensive performance from the Dortmund defence, including one memorable moment when substitute Serhou Guirassy’s determination to block a cross prompted a double ricochet off his own post. One could make the argument that there were times when it was “unbelievable”, as Arteta later said, that the ball did not find its way in. Although there were also moments when the reasons were self-evident.

“There’s an element of luck,” the Arsenal manager said, “and there is an element of us finishing better.”.

Industry observers note that in fifth place in the league phase table, dropped points at home do not carry the same jeopardy in the group stage that they once did, yet even so there was a truth for Arteta to chew upon. This is a well-honed, significant-game Arsenal Champions League side that he has built. One that reached the final last season and may well go close again, but as ever they seem to be doing so in spite of the great goalscorer that so many of their nearest rivals have at their disposal.

Arteta sounded that warning after defeat in the final in Budapest at the end of May and while changes have been made, it would be hard to argue that they have been fundamental. This was a good opponent – the leaders of the Bundesliga with many exports from English football who have been reconditioned for the German game. Those include Fábio Silva, Felix Nmecha and Jobe Bellingham who had a second-half goal narrowly disallowed for offside.

Jobe Bellingham's goal RULED OUT for offside ❌ https://t.co/yaR8EX4Gs3.

Industry observers note that after a chastening first half in which they found themselves in the teeth of the Arsenal press, Dortmund re-emerged as a much more effective attacking force. They found a way to break the Arsenal press by targeting Christos Tzolis and the run from the teenage French defender Joane Gadou that followed was exceptional. That created the goal for Beier, one of four shots on target from Dortmund – the same number as Arsenal.

Maximilian Beier punishes Arsenal to make it 1-1 😳 https://t.co/OOUmg9JnHo.

According to recent reports, dortmund, managed by the West German-born Croat Niko Kovac, did not always have Arsenal’s polish in possession but they certainly had the youth in their legs to match the English champions. In defence their captain Nico Schlotterback and Waldemar Anton will not have many better games. They might have been fortunate at times but they will also point to a penalty that was not given, when Gyokeres handled in his own area at the start of the second half.

According to recent reports, gyokeres’ first-half goal was certainly among the best he has scored for the club, invited to shoot by a Dortmund defence that simply stood off as he reached the edge of the area. He will not catch many as full as he did this one. More of a dig than a swish but with the useful consequence of packing a lot of power and a dip that meant goalkeeper Gregor Kobel saw it but could not pick out its flight.

It has been revealed that viktor Gyökeres what a HIT! 👏🔥 https://t.co/5m6FZoE8tQ.

Asked about the later Gyokeres miss, Arteta preferred to talk about other aspects of his striker’s performance. “The way he held up the ball, the way he threaded in behind and stretched the pitch,” Arteta mentioned. “There was a lot to like in that performance and that’s the Viktor that we needed.”.

Even so, there was some of the Gyokeres the Arsenal manager does not need as early as the end of the first half when he launched a wild shot over from Noni Madueke’s pass. Arteta was without David Raya who has a shoulder injury and there were no guarantees that he will be back for the Manchester City game on Sunday.

According to recent reports, some good moments for young Bellingham against Myles Lewis-Skelly in the first half and then a goal disallowed after the break. That came after Beier’s equaliser when Dortmund were at their counter-attacking best. In the final stages, Arsenal pressed hard for the equaliser and although there were lots of shots it would be hard to say there were lots of chances. The one that got away was the one that fell to Gyokeres.

Arteta would later call it “a brilliant performance”. It was hard to shake the feeling from some of the caveats he added that, like everyone else, what he really thought – above all – was that his team should have won.

Industry observers note that the performance was superb and there is no question about that from the start to the end. We played against a really good side and the domination and threat was really impressive. The general feeling inside the dressing room is that we should reward ourselves with more.

I love the courage, the fluidity and the understanding with the players with and without the ball.

That’s what we want [to finish in the top eight]. We have a big game against Manchester City at home on Sunday so we need to recover really well, we have four days to do that and sustain that momentum the way we are playing and the win will come.

According to recent reports, I think these are the best games. I’m really looking forward to it. Two draws on the bounce now and I just desperately want to win on the weekend and I know my team-mates feel the same. We are going to do everything we have to win the three points. We’re champions, we’re at home. We have a duty to perform well at the Emirates. There are things we need to improve but all in all we are going in the right direction.

Recent findings suggest that I feel like the performances from us up until the last shot was incredible at times. Definitely feels like two points dropped like the other day so, having dominated so much of the game we need to take all the points.

I prefer this type of game [more open rather than against a deep defence], there are more breaks and opportunities to attack space. We it’s a low block it’s more about pass, pass, pass and wait for the right moment. I feel like we are well-suited to both types of game.

We could have scored in the second half. We could have won the game in many different ways. We played well and created a lot of chances, we deserved to win the game but sometimes it is like that.

The most important thing is that we create those chances and get shots on goal. For sure we will score goals when games are coming up.

But they are now four points off Real Madrid, who they play next, and more than likely PSG if they beat Roma tomorrow night.

Arsenal with a remarkable combination of poor finishing and bad decision-making in the final third. They ended the night with 56 touches in the Dortmund box and 29 shots, but only four of those shots were on target.

There was time for one late scramble, but at the final whistle it is the Borussia Dortmund fans celebrating the draw.

Recent findings suggest that that result is going to make it very difficult for Arsenal to finish in the top two, but they will hope to have enough for a top-eight finish. They fail to win at home for the first time this season.

Dortmund had their moments, a very strong start to the second half when they could have scored more than once.

But over the piece, the story is Arsenal’s profligacy. Twenty nine shots on goal and more than two expected goals, but not enough to show for it.

Eze with a blocked shot but Arsenal do have Dortmund pushed back in their half for the final 90 seconds. Is there one more chance!

In a recent development, kobel palms behind Rice’s delivery for another Arsenal corner. Feels like now or never if Arsenal are to find the winner.

Promising attack for Dortmund, but Timber blocked Karestas’s shot.

Then Arsenal go down the other end and win a corner through Hincapie’s persistence.

Just four minutes of added time.

Gabriel tries to win a header on the edge of Dortmund’s box but gives a foul away. Odegaard’s shot was blocked in the build up, he may have been better off crossing to the back post.

Sources indicate that arsenal with some good football through the lines involving Odegaard and Bruno Guimaraes, but then Konsa was the wrong man in the wrong place and committed a foul. Mikel Merino has replaced Viktor Gyokeres.

Some of the venom has gone out of the Arsenal backlash since the equaliser, but they continue to probe and push numbers forward.

Industry observers note that and Declan Rice hits the post! Brilliant slide-rule pass from Eze to release Rice into the box, and his first-time shot with his left foot cannons of the near post.

Dortmund have a throw deep in the Arsenal half now, after Kepa found himself in a tight spot and kicked to touch. Arsenal clear but Eze fails to bring them up the pitch.

Scramble in the Dortmund goal-mouth from an Arsenal free-kick, whipped in low by Odegaard right across the face of goal, kept alive by Hincapie at the back post and the ball bounced off the post when it looked like being an own goal. Kobel stays down to receive some treatment after colliding with the post.

It feels like Arsenal have restored some dominance since the changes, and after some messy play in the penalty box they have a corner. Punched clear by Kobel, before Madueke is fouled.

Arsenal crowd growing a little frustrated with Odegaard for turning down a shot at the edge of the box, and also failing to find Gyokeres with the pass.

Then Gyokeres misses a sitter! Brilliant ball from Odegaard, Gyokeres completely unmarked to meet to inswinging cross but he heads wide from six yards. Hincapie’s run maybe put him off but that would be generous.

Eze with a sloppy giveaway in his own half but Arsenal are not punished, before Rice sets the home team away with some great play in midfield. Eze feeds Gyokeres down the left, but not red player was in the six-yard box for a cross.

Then Madueke cuts inside from the right and shoots not far wide of the near post.

According to recent reports, arsenal’s inability to control this second half has made for a very entertaining game. Two teams going for it. Dortmund seem to accept they can’t defend their way to a result so they might as well try to attack.

It has been revealed that arsenal respond by throwing a couple of punches. First Eze’s shot was deflected over, before Anton made a magnificent block to deny Madueke. The game is swinging back and forth.

Industry observers note that jobe Bellingham wheels away in celebration thinking he has scored for Dortmund after Ryerson’s shot was saved from Kepa but the flag goes up for offside! It took Bellingham ages to realise, and his joy was cut short.

Recent findings suggest that replays show it was very, very tight indeed. The still image suggested Hincapie was playing him on, but VAR confirms offside as the decision.

To give Kepa credit, it was a sharp save.

Gyokeres with more gallant work in the channels for Arsenal but he is lacking some support at times, perhaps Eze and Guimaraes can change that.

Triple sub from Arsenal: Eze, Guimaraes and Timber replace Tzolis, Lewis-Skelly and White.

It has been revealed that anton looks short of pace at the back for Dortmund, and Gyokeres streaks away from him down the left. Hincapie is the player found with the cut-back, and he tees up White for a shot that is always rising.

The Greek winger allowed Gadou to burst away and then dived in ineffectively as he ran downfield. These are the details and duels that Arteta obsesses over.

According to recent reports, goudou with a burst away from Tzolis and straight through the middle of the Arsenal midfield, and Beier’s first touch inside Gabriel was fantastic before he finished with a left-footed shot into the bottom corner. A very well-worked equaliser.

That’s how to break the Arsenal press. Run hard at Tzolis and give it everything. Great finish from Beier but an even better run from Joane Gadou to make it.

Maximilian Beier punishes Arsenal to make it 1-1 😳 https://t.co/OOUmg9JnHo.

Looking back at the penalty shout, Gyokeres’ arm was slightly away from his body.

Cleared by Ben White at the near post, but there were loud Dortmund appeals for a handball penalty.

A 70mph strike from Viktor Gyökeres against Dortmund 💨😮‍💨 https://t.co/hQHcCWvjUz.

Noni Madueke has started nine of Arsenal's last 11 matches in all competitions. This run of games has had such a positive effect on him. He looks more confident, relaxed and expressive than at any point in his #AFC career. Perhaps not having the pressure of Saka has helped him.

Industry observers note that dortmund’s gameplan clearly based on the build-up from goalkeeper to the two centre-halves and then forward. It is a different prospect doing it in the Bundesliga to doing it against the Arsenal pressing machine and over the course of the first half Dortmund have lost their nerve in that regards. Goalkeeper Gregor Kobel has gone long to the left flank more than he would have liked. But – and it’s a significant point – they have looked quite good once they have got into Arsenal’s half. The Gyokeres goal was a good dig that beat Kobel with the dip. It was close to him. For all that Gyokeres was invited to shoot. Not a yellow shirt near by.

Arsenal much the better team across the 45 minutes, racking up 14 shots and enjoying 61 per cent possession. A familiar tale though, is their failure to convert that dominance into a commanding lead. Borussia Dortmund gradually carried more threat as the half progressed, and Arsenal cannot count on the insurance policy of Raya in goal. They need the second goal.

Industry observers note that A moment of sloppiness from Arsenal near the end of the half, and Kepa was almost caught out at his near post but managed to make the save at the expense of a corner. Nmecha won first contact, but his header looped over.

Kepa patient on the ball for Arsenal to find Gabriel, who picks out Madueke with a diagonal over the top. Good close control from the winger, and he tees up Gyokeres for another attempt from just outside the box but he skies this one.

According to recent reports, dortmund win a corner from another Ryerson cross, he has looked their best outlet down the right. From the corner, Kepa was scrambling among bodies but Arsenal get away with it. Arteta wanted a foul on the goalkeeper.

Recent findings suggest that dortmund are a far more open opponent than Arsenal are used to facing in the Premier League, and they are fortunate not to have conceded more goals here, but they are willing to attack quite quickly in numbers. They’ve had five shots so far, and a couple of those were decent chances.

From the second phase of the next corner, Tzolis volleyed miles over when a shot was not on. Lewis-Skelly has been quietly effective in midfield for Arsenal, and there is applause for Ethan Nwaneri as he goes out to warm up for Dortmund. William Saliba is also out there stretching.

Incisive from Odegaard after Dortmund lost the ball in a dangerous position, and Rice charged straight through the middle, but was running out of steam as he took the shot and it deflected wide.

Corner taken short, well-worked between Lewis-Skelly and Tzolis, and the caught back falls for Gyokeres whose shot deflects wide for another corner.

No doubt Arsenal’s electric start of the opening 15 minutes has slowed, I’m not sure it would be possible or desirable to maintain that intensity across the 90 minutes. They are controlling the pace of and remaining patient, before Rice lets fly from almost 30 yards. Not far over the bar.

Dortmund with a nifty up, set and through but they had run offside. Gabriel then looks over the top for Hincapie, who was running over the top like a striker from left-back yet again.

Declan Rice with a crunching tackle in his own half that has the Emirates crowd on its feet, and Arsenal are flowing forward into space again but Gyokeres failed to pick the right final ball.

Now Dortmund have a corner after a Svensson shot deflects wide. Kepa claims with ease.

Industry observers note that hincapie, as we have seen with Arsenal’s full-backs all season, is popping up in advanced positions and he had a clear sight of goal but elected to pull the ball back when he should have put his laces through it. Well worked attack before then though, with Rice finding Odegaard between the lines and Gyokeres flicking the ball around the corner.

Better again from Dortmund, moving the ball with fluency from their own defensive third but Nmecha miscues his shot over the bar from the edge of the box. Kepa is then off his line to collect a chipped ball over the top.

Tzolis did well to harry and win the race to a long ball forward and he was close to flicking the ball into the path of Gyokeres.

Industry observers note that dortmund are starting to string some passes together, and they have a corner. This is one department where Arsenal will be appreciably worse without Raya but Hincapie heads clear.

Madueke then spins into space on the break and Gyokeres is free in the middle, but the winger slices the chipped pass.

Dortmund with their first attempt of the night after Ryerson swung in a cross from the left. Lewis-Skelly did well to compete in the air with Bellingham, before Silva kicked fresh air. Then with his second attempt, he volleyed over the bar.

Sources indicate that dortmund trying to settle into a spell of possession, but every pass feels like a chore for them at the moment and they are caught offside. Arsenal’s task now is to score the second while they have Dortmund where they want them. The German side will surely have a spell.

Sources indicate that gyokeres with another stretching run beyond Schlotterbeck, who is not the quickest. Arsenal completely dominant at the moment, but they do not always capitalise on these spells.

Chance for a second! Tzolis’ shot was parried by Kobel and Madueke’s rebound was blocked after he took a beat to control the ball. Could Madueke taken a swing first time?

Industry observers note that arsenal are well worth that opening goal. Looking back at the replays of Gyokeres’s strike, it was an unusual technique, brushing the turf before the ball much as a golfer might do with a bunker shot.

Gyokeres may lack craft at times but there is no doubt he has power. That was a superb strike, dipping towards goal with real ferocity. Arsenal don’t score many goals from range but they have plenty of players who can do it. Gyokeres now has five goals and three assists in his last 10 games for club and country.

Industry observers note that madueke in acres of space down the right again, and there was too much space in front of the Dortmund back three for Gyokeres to receive the ball and turn. From there, Gyokeres decided to take the shot on and his laces technique produced power and dip which deceived the goalkeeper Kobel. It was not in the corner, but the loop did for him. According to recent reports, dortmund find themselves beyond the halfway line for the first time in the game and there was an error from Rice that Fabio Silva failed to take advantage of. Arsenal soon back on the front foot though, and Odegaard’s shot from distance is blocked.

It has been revealed that noni Madueke has been Arsenal’s best attacker in recent weeks and he has started well here. He is really thriving in the absence of the injured Bukayo Saka. Perhaps that knowledge that he will start games has given him a sense of freedom that he was lacking before.

Industry observers note that arsenal have endured some slow starts to matches this season, but this has not been one of them. Dortmund cannot find room to breathe at the moment, and Arsenal are moving the ball with speed and authority. They are up the pitch again after Gyokeres wins a foul. Moments earlier, Madueke found Tzolis at the back post with a curling cross but Dortmund cleared his nod across goal.

Gyokeres with a scuffed shot from long range straight at the goalkeeper, but Arsenal continue to be on the front foot. Hincapie, their left-back challenged for the ball in the centre-forward position.

Very positive start from Arsenal, enjoying all of the ball in the first few minutes. Tzolis with a promising cross which was not far away from Hincapie, then Lewis-Skelly was in well to keep Dortmund pinned back. Madueke was found in space, and Tzolis connected with his ball to the back post, the volley bouncing over the ball.

Dortmund get the game under way, and line up almost all of their team on the left side of the pitch.

The entrance of players follows a pre-match light show and an airing of everyone’s favourite song The Angel, shunted back in the schedule to make room for the Champions League anthem.

You can see Jobe is developing very well. As you also saw, he is now part of the England national team now.

This is not by random, this is because he deserves it and he plays very well in the Bundesliga. Since he arrived, he’s developed day after day.

Recent findings suggest that in the beginning he needed a bit of time because the differences between the Championship and Bundesliga are huge, also the cultural aspect is different. He came to a latest country, he had to learn now to live in Germany, but he’s there.

I’m very happy with him. He’s progressing and not only developing physically but with the ball and this is what we need.

I’m very impressed with them, with what Niko has done with the team, especially the way they are playing, the way they are dominating games, the amount of threat that they are able to create.

We had them here in pre-season (a 3-2 defeat) and they showed their quality and what they are capable of, so we are very much aware of that.

But we play at home in front of our crowd and we’re going to go and attack the game, that’s for sure.

Industry observers note that mikel Arteta seems quite set on his left-back pecking order: Riccardo Calafiori starts on weekends, and Piero Hincapie starts in midweek. They are very different players (Calafiori is the more adventurous, while Hincapie is more of an old-school defender) and it seems that Arteta feels Hincapie is better suited to Champions League football. He’ll be tested tonight against the Bundesliga leaders.

Recent findings suggest that by Yannick HuberOn Tuesday, all eyes will be on Ethan Nwaneri. The Champions League clash between Arsenal and Borussia Dortmund marks the 19-year-old’s return to the club where he grew up, where he became the Premier League’s youngest player and from whom he joined Dortmund on loan in the summer. It would be hard to imagine a more poignant setting. But for Nwaneri, facing Arsenal is about more than a reunion. It is also an opportunity to finally make his mark at Dortmund.

So far his time in Germany has not gone according to plan. Nwaneri arrived with a considerable reputation and high expectations, but has become less prominent in recent weeks. His playing time has diminished and he has frequently had to settle for a place on the bench.

But there are several reasons to believe that, of all games, this meeting with his former club could give his Dortmund career fresh impetus.

Arsenal: Kepa; White, Konsa, Gabriel, Hincapie; Rice, Lewis-Skelly; Madueke, Odegaard, Tzolis; GyokeresSubs: Meslier, Porter, Saliba, Mosquera, Eze, Timber, Merino, Havertz, Calafiori, Guimaraes, Dowman.

Dortmund: Kobel, Ryerson, Anton, Schlotterbeck, Gadou, Svensson, Veerman, Nmecha, Bellingham, Beier, SilvaSubs: Drewes, Meyer, Bensebaini, Guirassy, Chukwuemeka, Nwaneri, Karetsas, Sabitzer, Mane, Albert, Dos Santos, Reggiani.

Mikel Arteta was an Arsenal player the last time they played Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League, and tonight he will have to make do without first-choice goalkeeper David Raya.

Arsenal’s manager struck an upbeat note when describing the shoulder or upper arm injury Raya sustained at Newcastle, and it appears he has avoided a long-term absence.

Recent findings suggest that even two weeks out, however, would mean Raya missing Premier League fixtures against Manchester City, Brentford and Spurs – possibly Arsenal’s most testing week of the season. Arteta did not rule out a return to face City on Sunday.

In a recent development, kepa Arrizabalaga is expected to deputise against Dortmund, who are top of the Bundesliga and have won three of their four Champions League league phase games. They won at the Emirates in a pre-season friendly, and Jobe Bellingham and on-loan Arsenal attacker Ethan Nwaneri are among their ranks.

These Champions League fixtures can feel secondary in importance to Premier League fare because of the competition’s new format, but a top-two finish in the league phase is a serious incentive.

As Arsenal discovered to their benefit last season when they “won” the league phase, the top two teams are rewarded with home second legs all the way to the final.

Arsenal are currently third on 10 points and face Real Madrid at the Emirates next, the team above them in second, so victory this evening is essential to set up that occasion.

Arteta has tended to make between four and six changes for these games, and Ben White, Piero Hincapie, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Christos Tzolis and Viktor Gyokeres are players pushing for starts after starting on the bench at Newcastle.

Also among the substitutes at St James’ Park was William Saliba, who is stepping up his return from a long-term back injury and could play his first minutes of the season tonight.

Editor’s Note:  Dean Obeidallah, a former attorney, is the host of SiriusXM radio’s daily program “The Dean Obeidallah Show.” Follow him @DeanObeidallah@masto.ai. The opinions expressed in this commentary are his own. View more opinion on CNN.

Industry observers note that last year, GOP Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene of Georgia spoke at a white nationalist event organized by Holocaust denier Nick Fuentes that caused Republican leaders to denounce her.

Last week, Greene’s Twitter account was temporarily suspended by the Elon Musk-headed platform over a tweet with a graphic referring to a “Trans Day of Vengeance,” as she denounced a planned transgender rights rally.

And come Tuesday, Greene has confirmed plans to protest in Newly introduced York City when former President Donald Trump is expected to be arraigned on an indictment of more than 30 counts, calling the proceedings against him an “unconstitutional WITCH HUNT!”.

But on Sunday, Greene was featured on CBS’ “60 Minutes” in an interview the long-running show promoted on Twitter with the tease: “Republican Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene, nicknamed MTG, isn’t afraid to share her opinions, no matter how intense and in-your-face they are. She sits down with Lesley Stahl this Sunday on 60 Minutes.” The images attached to this tweet by “60 Minutes” include Greene and Stahl walking through the US Capitol, taking a stroll outside and Greene showing Stahl something on her phone.

It's time for Marjorie Taylor Greene to go.

Industry observers note that in the segment that aired Sunday night, Stahl noted the congresswoman had moved from the fringe to the GOP’s front row in two years despite a “sharp tongue” and “some pretty radical views” as well as “over the top” comments such as “the Democrats are a party of pedophiles.” Stahl also referred to video of Greene chasing a Parkland, Florida, school shooting survivor, still maintaining that the 2020 election was stolen and failing to criticize Trump over spending. (The interview was conducted before news of his indictment.).

But Stahl didn’t mention Greene spoke at a white nationalist event a year ago while a member of Congress or her extreme anti-Muslim views and her defense of January 6 rioters.

It has been revealed that criticism of CBS for amplifying Greene has been swift and well-deserved even before the program aired. Former GOP Rep. Adam Kinzinger of Illinois tweeted beforehand: “Wow. Insane that 60 min would do this.” (Kinzinger is a CNN senior political commentator.).

Journalist Molly Jong-Fast also slammed “60 Minutes” with the tweet: “Attention is currency and 60 minutes is spending its currency on the Jewish space lasers woman.” (Jong-Fast was apparently referring to Greene’s past claim that a massive California wildfire was started by “a laser” beamed from space controlled by a prominent Jewish banking family.).

David Hogg, who survived the 2018 horrific school shooting at Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in Parkland and has since become an activist against gun violence, responded, “I look forward to your questions about why she thinks school shootings are fake and why she’s supported QAnon.”.

Trump's risky call for protests.

In a recent development, greene amplified the conspiracy theory — two years before being elected to Congress — that the Parkland shooting that took 17 lives was staged. And in 2019, Greene appeared on video confronting Hogg outside the Capitol when he was championing laws to save lives from gun violence, screaming that the then-teenager was a “coward.” She also called Hogg “#littleHitler” on social media.

Industry observers note that greene’s own tweet promoting Sunday’s segment was not filled with her typical smears of “fake news” when she doesn’t like the coverage. Rather, Greene urged people to tune in as she praised “60 Minutes” host Stahl (and misspelled her first name): “It was an honor to spend a few days with the legendary icon Leslie Stahl and talented crew @60Minutes.” Greene added, “Leslie is a trailblazer for women in journalism. And while we may disagree on some problems, I respect her greatly.”.

Recent findings suggest that now, it is true that “60 Minutes” over its 50-plus-year history has featured what the show has dubbed “controversial” guests. These include a 2000 interview with Oklahoma City bomber Timothy McVeigh, whose 1995 terrorist attack left 168 dead, including 19 children. And the show did a 1979 interview with Iran’s Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini.

Perhaps “60 Minutes” views Greene — who has repeatedly downplayed and even defended the January 6, 2021, attack plus called for the GOP to become the party of “Christian nationalism” — in the vein of its long list of controversial guests. (CBS had not responded to a request from CNN for comment at time of publishing.).

Join us on Twitter and Facebook.

However, the choice of Greene as a guest instantly recalls the comments of then-CBS CEO Les Moonves during Trump’s 2016 presidential campaign when he admitted that Trump’s candidacy “may not be good for America, but it’s damn good for CBS.” Moonves added, “The money’s rolling in and this is fun. … (T)his is going to be a very good year for us,” concluding, “Sorry. It’s a terrible thing to say. But bring it on, Donald. Keep going.”.

Moonves may be gone from CBS, but it appears his mindset continues at “60 Minutes.” And that may be good for “60 Minutes,” but it’s definitely not good for America.

Man United furious with Howard Webb over support for Leny Yoro red card

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Manchester United are furious after referees’ chief Howard Webb backed the decision to send off Leny Yoro against Liverpool, despite the defender successfully having his one-match suspension rescinded.

It has been revealed that the 21-year-old French centre-back received his marching orders just eight minutes into United’s 4-0 defeat at Anfield on Sunday for a challenge on Reds forward Alexander Isak. Referee Sam Barrott ruled that Yoro had denied an obvious goalscoring opportunity and VAR decided against overturning the on-field decision.

United successfully appealed against the decision for wrongful dismissal, and the Football Association has confirmed the ban has been lifted, clearing Yoro to feature in Saturday’s Premier League match against Brentford at Old Trafford.

Liverpool opened the scoring straight from the free-kick awarded following Yoro’s foul.

In a recent development, debate had centered on whether Isak possessed sufficient control of the ball for the incident to count as the denial of an obvious goalscoring opportunity. The Swedish international's touch ran through into the arms of United goalkeeper Senne Lammens.

Pro Ref’s chief refereeing officer Webb supported the decision to dismiss the player, arguing it was "certainly not clearly wrong".

However, United boss Mauricio Pochettino strongly disagreed with the call and criticised the absence of VAR intervention.

It is understood that the club are angry with Webb’s remarks and intend to express their feelings directly to Pro Ref.

Industry observers note that speaking at a press conference ahead of his team’s Champions League match against Sporting in Lisbon on Wednesday, the Argentinian stated: "Very disappointed. My question always was the same, we can accept the referee can make a mistake because of the emotion of the game, sometimes the view or the position can affect that. But if we have VAR, what were they doing?

According to recent reports, "Now, are we going to repeat the game? Are we going to have the possibility to play with similar tools – 11 v 11?

According to recent reports, "We have an unbelievable car, but we need to have the level to drive, we need to drive in the best way. We love the technology, yes, and we accept the technology is there, but what are they doing? But it’s not only this mistake, it affects everything.

"No-one is talking about the (Dominik Szoboszlai’s) goal wasn’t legal, they should have disallowed the goal because (Bradley) Barcola was touching our wall. Maybe in the last two years the rules have changed while I was in America. Why didn’t they check it? It must be disallowed.".

Webb addressed the dismissal during an interview with former Liverpool and United striker Michael Owen on the latest episode of Match Officials: Mic’d Up, which was broadcast on Tuesday evening but filmed before the FA confirmed Yoro’s suspension was overturned.

"The reason we’re talking about it is the fourth consideration (in DOGSO decisions), that’s control or likelihood of keeping or gaining control of the ball," Webb noted.

"Isak’s got control of the ball, he’s got possession, he’s got the touch, he knocks it past Yoro. He’s moving at pace at that moment and a crowd comes in and knocks him down.

"There’s a question mark I guess around whether or not he would get onto that ball before Lammens. Now, in the moment, the referee looked at it and felt he would.

"The VAR checks to see whether that decision made on the field was clearly and obviously incorrect, and formed the opinion that it wasn’t.

"I think by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving promptly on towards that ball. The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it’s a little bit debatable. (It’s) certainly not clearly wrong.".

VAR John Brooks shared that view, telling referee Barrott in the released audio: "Let’s roll it through firstly to see whether the attacker is going to get on the end of the ball.

It has been revealed that "Just roll through real speed. So, at full speed, Isak maintains his momentum and likely gets on the end of it.

In a recent development, "OK, certainly not clearly wrong that he doesn’t. So I think the DOGSO confirmed.".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, the newly introduced report focuses on China, Russia and the emerging space powers of Iran and North Korea.
  • Industry observers note that the report — the 2026 edition of "Challenges to Security in Space" — is the third iteration of the DIA's unclassified intelligence assessment on space-related challenges and threats to U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, last month, the U.S. Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) released a chilling and info-packed report judging the scope and breadth of threats posed by the nation's adversaries in space.

In a recent development, the newly introduced report focuses on China, Russia and the emerging space powers of Iran and North Korea. It looks at what's happening in Earth orbit and beyond, including cislunar space, the region between our planet and the moon.

Industry observers note that the report — the 2026 edition of "Challenges to Security in Space" — is the third iteration of the DIA's unclassified intelligence assessment on space-related challenges and threats to U.S. national security, as well as the extent to which space is treated internationally as a warfighting domain.

Information within the report, which you can read here, is current as of July 2026. DIA's mission is to provide intelligence on foreign militaries to help prevent wars, and win the ones that are fought.

The report's up-front finding is that China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea are developing, testing, deploying and using space capabilities "in a way that threatens the security of all space systems and their associated space benefits.".

Indeed, China and Russia are developing "a formidable spectrum" of offensive capabilities to degrade or destroy space services of other countries, from kinetic destruction to sophisticated jamming and cyber operations.

The DIA report also notes that "the production of cheaper, smaller, and simpler satellites, which are faster to develop and deploy, along with the expansion of commercially available launch services, are driving the rapid integration of commercial space alternatives to support national security.".

While space commercialization is making previously government-centered space services widely available to interested parties, the DIA report adds, that availability also includes state and non-state actors with malign interests.

A major item dealt with by the DIA is "counterspace" — and it's not the kind that you'll find in your kitchen.

Counterspace operations can be either offensive or defensive. They can be used on purpose to reversibly or irreversibly deny, disrupt, degrade, damage or destroy a space object or component of a space system.

Here are the key elements of counterspace, as identified within the DIA report:.

The DIA report underscores that Russia is developing a satellite designed to carry a nuclear weapon.

It has been revealed that russia is doing so despite its obligation to comply with the 1967 Outer Space Treaty. That U.N. agreement prohibits the placement of any objects carrying nuclear weapons, or any other kinds of weapons of mass destruction, into orbit around Earth.

"A space-based capability such as this could cause rapid and sudden loss or degradation of thousands of satellites operated by countries and companies around the world," the DIA report states, "as well as to the vital communications, navigation, scientific, meteorological, commercial and national security services they provide.".

A nuclear detonation in space could be tailored to impact satellites in most orbits, the DIA report warns, from low Earth orbit for commercial and reconnaissance satellites, geosynchronous orbit for critical communications, and medium Earth orbit for navigation and timing satellites.

The newly issued DIA report also observes that exploring cislunar space is of increasing interest to spacefaring nations for potential scientific and economic opportunities. However, nations such as China "may be exploring military applications from cislunar space," the report notes.

China has stated its goal of developing a cislunar space economy by 2045.

"China is also the first country to attempt sustained operations on the far side of the moon, with numerous projects slated to support that effort through the next decade. China portrays its interest in cislunar space as peaceful, but PRC [People's Republic of China] officials have also discussed pursuing military capabilities in cislunar space," the report states.

Placing a keen eye on the DIA report is Peter Garretson, a senior fellow in defense studies at the American Foreign Policy Council and a strategy consultant who focuses on space and defense.

Sources indicate that according to Garretson, the most significant positive change from earlier DIA appraisals is the explicit assessment that Russia is developing a satellite designed to carry a nuclear weapon. He told Space.com that the DIA's expanded treatment of the threat of a nuclear weapon on orbit reflects concerns in the Congress and the Trump White House.

However, Garretson also flagged what he noted is a consequential omission in the report: the disappearance of the prior treatment (in the 2022 version of the report) of research competition, surveillance beyond geosynchronous Earth orbit and the potential military use of deep space for staging reserve forces.

In Garretson's view, the DIA needs to help put the puzzle pieces together for Congress and the attentive public about what exactly China is doing, and how it fits together in the nation's strategy to achieve comprehensive space dominance.

According to Garretson, "everything they are doing, from launch cadence, reusable launch, commercial space investment, investments in power, propulsion, repair, manufacturing, to commercial assets working together" supports both an economic expansion toward upcoming resources and what China hopes will be overwhelming military power and strategic depth.

Sources indicate that garretson senses the moves by China to develop extractive and in-space industries "is truly the strategic threat that could crush American space power. Now is the time to be making the investments to ensure we have a 'freedom's forge' and 'arsenal of democracy' in space that can protect the open space commerce that is the nation's strategy.".

As for the DIA's outlook for the future: The agency concluded that space almost certainly will remain an increasingly competitive and crowded environment as space capabilities improve and other countries seize opportunities in the final frontier.

"The increase of Chinese, Russian, Iranian and North Korean counterspace capabilities, rapid growth in the number of space objects, and the proliferation of requirements for space-enabled services," the DIA report states, "will all complicate operations in space in the coming decade.".

He also wrote "Mars: Our Future on the Red Planet" released in 2016 by National Geographic. Leonard  has served as a correspondent for SpaceNews, Scientific American and Aerospace America for the AIAA. He has received many awards, including the first Ordway Award for Sustained Excellence in Spaceflight History in 2015 at the AAS Wernher von Braun Memorial Symposium. Latest Update: The best European strikers this century - ranked by you

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2092 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • There is no one-size fits all when it comes to determining great strikers, but they do all share a common trait - a ruthlessness in front of goal.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The top 10 European strikers of the 21st century.

Classic number nines, penalty-box poachers, troublesome targetmen and tireless all-rounders.

There is no one-size fits all when it comes to determining great strikers, but they do all share a common trait - a ruthlessness in front of goal.

This week, however, we put the power in your hands to decide the best European frontmen of the 21st century.

Tens of thousands of you voted on the 20-man shortlist drawn up by our panel.

We then asked European football experts Guillem Balague, Julien Laurens and Raphael Honigstein to discuss your choices on the Euro Leagues podcast.

So from 10-1, here are the best European strikers this century - as voted for by you.

Top 10 European Strikers of the Century - Part One.

Karim Benzema comes in at number 10, the former Lyon and Real Madrid frontman's closest challengers coming from across the continent in the shape of Raul, Robin van Persie, Michael Owen and Miroslav Klose.

Laurens: "From a young age you could see he was something special. I know it was difficult at the beginning at Real Madrid, but in the post-Cristiano era he carried that team, wore the armband and won significant titles and trophies by being decisive in big moments. Like I used to say 'Karim the dream'.".

According to recent reports, honigstein: "The selflessness, the ability to work for the team. A sense of elegance and humility on the pitch, which is unusual in a goalscorer. I think he is unusual in that list. I think not many will define themselves through their teamwork and assists as much as their goals, but he was that player.".

Ruud van Nistelrooy edges Benzema, with whom he briefly overlapped at Real Madrid - the Dutchman teed up the Frenchman and scored himself in their only La Liga appearance together, before he left for Hamburg in January 2010 following injury problems.

The former PSV striker's most consistent spell, of course, came at Manchester United, where he scored 150 goals.

Honigstein: "He is the nicest guy but he never came across that way on the pitch. Typical trait of a striker, he would kill to score the goal. I think anyone who has grown up with him scoring goals, for United especially, must have a soft spot for him because he was a phenomenal poacher.".

Laurens: "He was a strong player physically, and despite the lack of pace the awareness in the box was just very special even with all the injuries.".

Industry observers note that zlatan Ibrahimovic slots in at eight, comfortably clear of Van Nistelrooy and Benzema. The Swede netted more than 500 times in a career that spanned Malmo, Ajax, Juventus, both Milans, Barcelona, Paris St-Germain, Manchester United and LA Galaxy.

It has been revealed that balague: "He was a big-game player and that explains the league titles with PSG. Scoring four goals against England, the overhead kick. The personality thing has put him one or two places in this list, saying 'I am great, I am the best'. If you keep saying you're great it makes people stop and think.".

Laurens: "The mentality of really believing he was the best and nobody was better than him, apart from maybe Brazilian Ronaldo, who was his idol growing up, and he would watch videos of him and try to replicate in his council estate. If you watch a highlight reel of his best goals he was incredible.".

Honigstein: "What makes him unique among the strikers is his technique, You could see elements of martial arts in his goals. No-one scores goals like that.".

The first Englishman on the list, although the third to have represented Manchester United - it's the Old Trafford outfit's record goalscorer, Wayne Rooney.

Recent findings suggest that honigstein: "I don't think there is anyone who would've watched English football at that time [early in his career] and not been enthralled by his game. The only downside is the combination of injuries and not the most professional lifestyle meant he did not fulfil his potential. He could've been Messi.".

Recent findings suggest that balague: "What could have been, yes. He was the national team's record scorer too before Harry Kane took it. I find him to deserve this place as he had to adapt to a lot of strikers and he did it well. He had the ability to link up and score. He was very intelligent.".

Sources indicate that laurens: "He is the most street footballer England has ever seen. There's no rules, that kind of anger you saw on the pitch. I don't think people in England realise how good he was.".

Industry observers note that what does becoming the all-time World Cup top goalscorer get you? Sixth place on the best European strikers this century list. The Real Madrid forward, 27, just misses out on the top five.

In a recent development, laurens: "Maybe if we do this ranking again in a few years he will be higher. I would have had him top five, for sure. He has scored more than 400 goals. I don't think Messi and Ronaldo had scored that many at that age, so he's ahead. I don't know if he will play for as long as them but he hasn't done much wrong in his career.".

Balague: "This list has to do what you feel about the player, not science - 22 goals in 22 appearances in World Cups and [Euro] Championships. He should be at least top three because of that. Great stats, but we're not in love with him.".

It has been revealed that honigstein: "I don't think there is a forward that is as good as footballer as him in 2026. On that basis alone he should be higher, but people when they vote have other things in their head. The only way to win everyone over is to score more goals and win more World Cups for France, which I think is possible.".

There was little between Mbappe and Erling Haaland, but it is Manchester City's prolific Norwegian who slips in at fifth. The 26-year-old has already scored more than 300 club goals and has a staggering 68 in 61 games for his country.

In a recent development, balague: "Mbappe should be higher than him. Haaland scored 52 goals in 53 games [in 2022-23], that is astonishing, but he's gone 11 finals without scoring. We're talking about the best. We're talking about what we see at the moment and what we see is someone who is calculated but in a more charming way. An ability to score we haven't seen in a while; power, ability to finish. He is not world class to the level of others.".

Recent findings suggest that honigstein: "I don't think it's fair to judge him on just that. They [Manchester City] won the Champions League when he was there. When Haaland arrived with Pep Guardiola, they found a way to do it. What makes him unique is the physical attributes and the pace. To have both is unique. He can sprint like a 100m sprinter. Is he the fifth best striker of the 21st Century? I don't think he's that far behind.".

Interesting, this, because Robert Lewandowski is well clear of Haaland in fourth, but the leap from the Polish forward to the top three is massive - more than 10,000 votes.

The 38-year-old is still chipping away for Chicago Fire in Major League Soccer, having been a reliably ruthless assassin for Barcelona, Bayern and Dortmund.

Honigstein: "He used to play basketball, judo, handball - his father wanted him to have a wholesome education. You could see his completeness that he had as a centre-forward. Nothing in his game was extraordinary but in terms of ticking all the boxes, none come close to him.".

Recent findings suggest that balague: "He remarked he learned to be an elite striker when he forgot what he had just done, like a fish. Mistakes he had in his head affected his performance. One day he just continued like it didn't matter.".

Laurens: "He won the Ballon d'Or in Covid, it won't be on his mantlepiece but we all know it was his.".

Fresh from his Ballon d'Or triumph, England's record goalscorer and appearance maker rides into the top three on the back of 61 goals in 51 outings for Bayern Munich last season.

Kane left the Premier League three years ago with the second-most goals ever in the competition, and is also Tottenham's all-time record scorer.

Sources indicate that honigstein: "Third place, at least. He is doing incredible things. At 33, still not quite at his peak. I don't think he relies on his pace, physicality, it's all about intelligence, technique. I don't think there's anyone in the game that strikes a ball as well as him right now. I don't think any player comes close that we've talked about so far in overall work-rate, defending, helping the team, making tackles in your box in the 90th minute when you're 3-0 up because he's that kind of guy. He is humble and a superb human being.".

In a recent development, laurens: "What I love about Kane, from a young age, a lot of this list you just knew the trajectory would be all the way to the top. Kane was not like that. It could have been very different for him. Nobody at 17 would've stated he was going to win the Ballon d'Or. Nobody believed in him like the others. Kane had a very different journey.".

Runner-up Thierry Henry is the only striker in the top six who is retired. A World Cup and Euros winner with France, Henry won titles with Arsenal - where he scored 228 goals - and a Champions League with Barcelona.

Honigstein: "During his time, I don't think there was a player like him in the Premier League. The way he played football was stylish, elegant, but there was almost a kind of a romantic connection between him and the ball. I don't think there was anyone near that kind of level of technique and, for want of a better word, va-va-voom he exuded. That just made for amazing viewing.".

It has been revealed that laurens: "For me as a fellow Parisien, he's a very special player, a very special man. A career that has been incredible from a young age. It's that season in the Premier League - 24 goals, 20 assists in 38 games - not even Kane or Benzema or Cristiano, OK, Messi is different, but they haven't done that and yet he did it.

Recent findings suggest that "There are still some people who undervalue him and underappreciate him and the monster that he was on the football pitch. He had it all. The pace, the style, the elegance, the technique, the mentality, the goals, the aura, the charisma. Just everything you wanted if you were to build a striker. One of the greatest football brains ever.".

Of course, at number one, it's the man chasing the 1,000-goal dream. Cristiano Ronaldo may have retired from Portugal duty with 146 notches on his strike chart but the quest goes on at Al-Nassr.

The 41-year-old's evolution from tricky winger to prolific frontman has taken him from Sporting to Manchester United, twice, Real Madrid, Juventus and now Saudi Arabia.

Balague: "He's the best striker in history. His numbers are incredible. He won't stop until he gets to 1,000. He is somebody who is special. We know his background, how he wanted to be Ballon d'Or winner at 12 and didn't stop until he got there. He ran up the mountains of Funchal with weights in his ankles and snuck into the gym when it was closed to get the physique he wanted.".

Laurens: "Always in the right place at the right time. The instinct. He was born with a gift, like all in this list. But you still have to work hard. Nobody will ever reach those levels again. 1,000 goals for club and country will never be done again, I think.".

According to recent reports, honigstein: "Peak Ronaldo for me was Gareth Bale scoring and him looking very unhappy. I don't think there will be any dispute about him being the greatest. Somebody who has done it all, won it all, and he's still going for the love of it.".

Where does Kane rank among all-time England greats?

#93845. Breaking: AI is ‘the end of mathematics as we know it’ — where does the field go next?

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1923 w)

Breaking: AI is ‘the end of mathematics as we know it’ — where does the field go next?

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1923 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that as the news spread from one mathematician to the next, panic set in.
  • Mathematicians astounded by AI and human-written proofs of iconic Riemann hypothesis.
  • Mathematicians astounded by AI and human-written proofs of iconic Riemann hypothesis.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that as the news spread from one mathematician to the next, panic set in. On 6 October, OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT, released more than 700 preprints written by AI, claiming to have solved more than 300 major open problems in mathematics. Some researchers stayed up all night combing through the papers that the organization had posted, anxious to know whether their entire research programmes had been rendered obsolete overnight.

Mathematicians astounded by AI and human-written proofs of iconic Riemann hypothesis.

Mathematicians astounded by AI and human-written proofs of iconic Riemann hypothesis.

Depending on who you ask, this was either the most progress or the most catastrophic development ever to happen in one day in the history of the field — or both. Either way, mathematicians realized that their profession would never be the same. “It’s probably the end of mathematics as we know it,” theoretical physicist Miranda Cheng remarked at an emergency meeting on mathematics and AI at the Royal Society in London in late October. Many of the papers cracked problems by combining ideas from disparate parts of the discipline, leveraging a universality of knowledge that no human could ever match — and leaving even some of the world’s smartest people feeling completely outdone.

Since then, one of the field’s greatest outstanding challenges, the Riemann hypothesis, also appears to have been solved with AI assistance. And mathematicians across the world have joined frantic collective efforts to confront challenges raised by AI’s advances, from how to evaluate and publish research papers to how to raise future generations of mathematicians. Some see the risk as existential. If mathematical problem-solving becomes mainly a machine endeavour — seen as a utility like water or electricity — then their profession could lose its status in society and human expertise might start to dwindle.

“It’s a challenge like we’ve never faced in mathematics — or in academia as a whole,” notes Simon Machado, a mathematician at the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology (ETH) in Zurich.

The bombshell paper drop in October came on the heels of earlier shocks to the field. OpenAI, which is based in San Francisco, California, released a batch of ten important results in August and, in early September, followed up with a historic solution to the Navier–Stokes problem about how fluids flow. The firm had been making noises to indicate that much more was to come. Still, many researchers were surprised by the enormity of the 6 October release. “To just see it as a giant list, without the care and thought and the love that goes into doing this work on a normal basis, it was really jarring,” indicates Catherine Cossaboom, a master’s student in mathematics at the University of Oxford, UK.

OpenAI posts 700 maths preprints online: mathematicians are up in arms.

OpenAI posts 700 maths preprints online: mathematicians are up in arms.

Perhaps no source has documented the moment better than Proofs and Prompts, an online forum that publishes essays on the impact of AI on mathematics. An 8 October post titled “100+ reactions to 100+ solutions” collected immediate reactions from dozens of students and career researchers to OpenAI’s 6 October drop. Some wrote poems, others quoted the writers Leo Tolstoy and Stanisław Lem, still others posted fragments from the Gospels (in the original Greek). One contribution reinterpreted the lyrics of ‘Jolene’ by the late country singer Dolly Parton:.

And I can easily understand / How you could easily take my math / But you don’t know what it means to me, AI.

In a recent development, the tone ranged from the enthusiastic to the angry and the despondent. “Some of them made me really feel heartbroken,” says Albane Théry, an applied mathematician at the University of Warwick in Coventry, UK, who is one of the volunteer moderators of the forum.

Sources indicate that few subfields of mathematics were spared and some were thoroughly ravaged. “Not a single one of the major open problems I have publicly mentioned throughout my career was left untouched,” Fields Medal winner Hugo Duminil-Copin wrote to Proofs and Prompts. “I expected that one day we would be surpassed, and that it would happen systematically. But yesterday’s announcement hit with a force I had not anticipated.”.

Hugo Duminil-Copin fears that AI will eclipse human understanding of mathematics.Credit: Chris Peus.

Industry observers note that duminil-Copin, who is at the University of Geneva in Switzerland, specializes in the theory of transitions in complex systems — such as those that determine how information or infection filters through social networks or how metals can acquire magnetization. (OpenAI’s rival Anthropic, also in San Francisco, had already claimed to have solved a major result in this field in late August.).

Sources indicate that another field that bore a massive impact was the theory of groups — some of the most ubiquitous structures across mathematics, physics and other disciplines. For example, the possible ways of shuffling a deck of cards — and what happens when you revert a shuffle or combine several together — constitute a group, as do the infinite possible ways of rotating a solid object in 3D.

OpenAI’s August batch already contained the solution to a key problem on groups. Soon after its release, during a YouTube interview, Francesco Fournier-Facio, a group theorist at Heriot-Watt University in Edinburgh, UK, mentioned two other problems that mathematicians could now attack with the help of AI. Within days, he was emailed by a PhD student in computational biology who had used OpenAI’s large language model (LLM) GPT 5.6 Sol to solve one of those problems.

In a recent development, can maths survive AI? Fields medallist Terence Tao calls for a ‘Maths 2.0’ world.

Can maths survive AI? Fields medallist Terence Tao calls for a ‘Maths 2.0’ world.

Fournier-Facio states that OpenAI’s October dump was even more impactful for him personally. It included the solution to a problem on which he had been actively working, called the Boone–Higman conjecture. Overall, OpenAI released solutions to perhaps eight of the top ten problems that Fournier-Facio had dreamed of solving during his career, he told Nature.

According to recent reports, but the most stunning AI result relates to what many researchers see as the most key open problem in all of mathematics. The Riemann hypothesis, a question that was posed in the mid-nineteenth century by the German mathematician Bernhard Riemann, centres on whether prime numbers are scattered across the set of all whole numbers in a way that is essentially as unpredictable as it could be.

Recent findings suggest that AI assistance seems to have cracked it. First, OpenAI proved a partial result, called the quasi-Riemann hypothesis, in its October dump. Then, on 20 November, Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge announced that he had found a proof of the full Riemann hypothesis, working with Claude, the firm’s AI assistant. However, that was swiftly followed by a non-AI assisted proof by Rome-based mathematician Alessandro Masullo, which he had been working on for years. “If this fully checks out, it is clearly a historic milestone in mathematics,” says number theorist James Maynard, a Fields Medal winner at the University of Oxford.

According to recent reports, maynard and many other researchers are excited by AI technology. It is “quite likely to unleash a golden age of mathematical discovery”, he remarked at the meeting. Another mathematician, Antoine Tilloy at the Mines Paris engineering school, part of PSL University, uses the metaphor that doing mathematics with AI is like riding a dragon: the researcher is still in charge, but the dragon gives them supernatural powers.

‘Mathematics is more than a mechanical process’ — why I think the field will survive OpenAI’s disruption.

‘Mathematics is more than a mechanical process’ — why I think the field will survive OpenAI’s disruption.

Industry observers note that but the speed at which AI proofs are emerging has already produced an immediate negative reaction. For one, mathematicians, who have long prided themselves on their field’s culture of openness, are now wary of discussing their work in public. “People are even scared to put out an abstract for a talk they are about to give on ongoing work,” notes Jakub Dobrowolski, a PhD candidate at Queen Mary University of London. “Nobody wants to share fresh ideas because of the speed at which somebody else can take them and write a paper,” says Peter Sarnak, a number theorist at Princeton University in New Jersey.

It has been revealed that and although established researchers say that they are both thrilled and anxious about reinventing their discipline with AI, younger generations are much more fearful. As Maynard and other established mathematicians acknowledge, the technology already poses severe problems in relation to how to assess merit when peer-reviewing mathematics work that might have been done mostly with AI, and how to train and educate the next generation of mathematicians.

It has been revealed that “How do we train people if a good PhD thesis can be prompted out of an LLM? The response from people who are in permanent positions tends to be ‘We’re going to see and discuss’,” says Théry. “But the timescale for that could be too long for postdoc or PhD candidates who will be out of a job in nine months.”.

It has been revealed that many early-career researchers told Nature that this uncertainty is their main source of anxiety right now. “While it is clear that faculty are working hard to find long-term solutions to the problems we are all facing, there doesn’t seem to be as much guidance on what to do in the meantime,” indicates Jad Hamdan, a postdoc mathematician at the University of Oxford. AI poses “more danger the younger you are, and the less experienced you are”, adds Dobrowolski. The toughest problem could be working out how to write a proposal for a research programme that might span two or three years, or more, Dobrowolski says. “Is it realistic? Now I feel like whatever I propose might just expire within a year.”.

Mathematicians are developing rules for AI use — other fields should follow.

Mathematicians are developing rules for AI use — other fields should follow.

A UK survey of graduate students and academic mathematicians last month by the Martingale Foundation in London found that PhD students in particular are much less optimistic about AI’s impact than are established researchers. Asked if AI would “weaken their development as mathematicians”, 89% of students agreed, compared with only 68% of academics.

#93843. Industry News: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1709 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1709 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ten games into the Premier League season, four of the top five places are occupied by 'substantial six' clubs.
  • Only second-placed Brighton, a club with a model which must be the envy of many of their rivals, and Premier League ever-presents Everton, have muscled their way in.
  • In pure financial terms, it should come as no surprise.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ten games into the Premier League season, four of the top five places are occupied by 'substantial six' clubs.

Only second-placed Brighton, a club with a model which must be the envy of many of their rivals, and Premier League ever-presents Everton, have muscled their way in.

In pure financial terms, it should come as no surprise.

The six biggest clubs - Manchester United, Liverpool, Manchester City, Arsenal, Tottenham and Chelsea - now generate hundreds of millions of pounds more than the division's other teams.

Recent findings suggest that and the gap is growing. Every season.

BBC Sport breaks down how the finances of the significant six have exploded, examines new trends and the impact on the transfer market, and asks how much it really matters.

Companies put their money where supporters are prepared to spend it. It is a simple fact of business in every country, a reality of football's food chain.

In England, Liverpool, Arsenal and Manchester United traditionally dominated viewing figures, column inches, shirt sales and sponsorship.

Over the past 20 years they have been joined by Chelsea, Manchester City and Tottenham.

This group of clubs now generate so much money it is hard to imagine how they can fail in the long term - even factoring in short-term performance issues.

Let's look at how the gap has grown.

We will use Everton, the only club not in the big six to be in the Premier League since its inception in 1992.

This tells a tale of how even one of the league's founding members can be left trailing well behind.

In 2009-10, the gap in revenues between the significant-six average and Everton was Â£120m. In 2024-25, that gap had grown to Â£442m.

So what has driven this huge escalation?

In large part it is the boom in international TV rights.

Kieran Maguire, professor of football finance at the University of Liverpool, told BBC Sport that it has attracted companies prepared to pay large sums to be associated with the Premier League's top clubs.

"The massive football brand clubs have global fanbases and that makes them very attractive to global commercial partners, especially for sponsorship and front-of-shirt deals," Maguire stated.

"You combine that with the fact that the Premier League is broadcast to 190 different countries around the world, and especially the international audiences - that allows the clubs to negotiate very good prices.".

Only 10% of Everton's revenue comes from commercial deals, while for the major six it is 45%.

It means Everton, and other clubs in the league, are heavily reliant on broadcast income. It makes up 66% of their revenue.

For Everton at least, this should change following the move to Hill Dickinson Stadium.

But that is unlikely to be enough to stop the gap increasing.

It has taken a few years, but Aston Villa and Newcastle have begun to increase their revenue.

This is largely thanks to the financial rewards of Champions League football.

But even Uefa has created a system which entrenches the position of the biggest clubs.

When the European Super League plan was torpedoed, Uefa created a new financial deal called the value pillar.

This reserves 35% of all Champions League revenues, or Â£713m, for the historically most successful clubs.

Industry observers note that at the end of the league phase last season City are estimated to have earned Â£37.9m from the value pillar, Liverpool Â£35.5m and Chelsea Â£33.3m. Newcastle received only Â£13.6m.

The good news for Villa is their coefficient has improved greatly, aided by last season's Europa League win.

Their value pillar is projected to be worth Â£25m this season. But that will still be less than the massive six clubs in the competition.

The cards are stacked against an ambitious club - not just domestically, but in Europe too.

Take a look at the financial trend of the major six and one thing becomes noticeable - Chelsea are beginning to fall behind.

In the past two seasons, and for the first time in recent history, the Blues recorded the lowest revenues of the massive six.

Sources indicate that not just by a small amount. They were Â£74m behind Tottenham, and Â£200m below Liverpool and Manchester City.

City's matchday income is the lowest, with the club's huge revenues largely due to commercial deals.

City, however, have been found guilty of breaching the Premier League financial rules between 2009-10 and 2017-18, inflating the value by using "sham contracts" with sponsors.

The club deny wrongdoing and have lodged an appealed against the verdict.

Chelsea's problem is simple - seats.

Stamford Bridge has a capacity of only 40,000, with no easy scope for expansion. The rest of the big six have grounds which hold at least 60,000.

Chelsea generated an average spend per fan of Â£80 in 2024-25, the second highest in the league after Arsenal.

Yet with 20,000 fewer tickets sold than their big six rivals, Chelsea's total matchday revenues are dwarfed.

Sources indicate that "Matchday spend has become increasingly crucial," Maguire remarked. "There has been a flatlining of broadcast revenues, especially since 2017.

"As a consequence, clubs have had to look at alternative methods of increasing revenues, especially with costs both on the pitch and off pitch rising so fast.".

Matchday revenue has effectively stalled for Chelsea, rising only Â£16m over the past 10 years. United's has grown by Â£69m and Spurs, thanks to their latest ground, by Â£85m.

"Chelsea are far more reliant upon player sales," Maguire said. "There is a growing divide because the global appeal is very much aligned with three or four clubs.

"Arsenal have re-established themselves with their progress in the Champions League. Manchester United are a brand in their own right. And Liverpool have expanded Anfield from 44,000 to 61,000, with many of those extra seats having gone to commercial.".

Chelsea's successful player trading model has so far limited the impact.

But there are signs that, financially at least, the substantial six could become the big five.

You might recall that Villa and Newcastle were not fans of the old profit and sustainability rules (PSR).

PSR forced both clubs to sell some of their best players to balance the books.

That has changed this season with squad-cost ratio (SCR).

There is a key difference with SCR, in that it allows a club to spend the money they generate on players. PSR limited losses so was more restrictive.

It has been revealed that "This does make it a little easier for the likes of Villa and Newcastle to spend money," Maguire said. "But it is still heavily weighted in favour of the substantial six.

"SCR is different to PSR rather than better. For some people, change is advantageous. For others, it isn't.".

The significant six generate hundreds of millions of pounds more than the other clubs. So they can spend hundreds of millions of pounds more on their squads.

This makes the big six even more powerful in the transfer market.

"Look at the clubs who voted against SCR - Brighton, Brentford, Bournemouth, Crystal Palace, Fulham and Leeds," Maguire said.

"It's very noticeable that those clubs have traditionally been very good at player sales, while they have tended to have lower matchday and commercial revenues.".

Most of the big six - the outlier being Chelsea - are not remotely close to the Premier League's 85% SCR limit.

Recent findings suggest that if you give clubs more money to spend on transfers, the likelihood is they will do just that. And the numbers back that up.

Premier League clubs spent Â£3.5bn - not only a highest total for a summer window, but it almost smashed the record for a whole season, the Â£3.53bn set in 2025-26.

The annual accounting cost of previous transfers, or amortisation, has been rising year on year.

"Over the course of the last decade, transfer amortisation has more than doubled and close to tripled," Maguire said.

"Which means that on average, clubs in the Premier League are now spending, or now have a cost which goes into their SCR calculations of just under Â£100m.".

Uefa fears that SCR will make matters worse, and have an inflationary impact across Europe.

And you can see why it is concerned.

In the summer 13 Premier League clubs broke their transfer record.

Brentford, Brighton, Palace, Leeds and Nottingham Forest all spent more than Â£40m on a player - unthinkable until recently.

So we have learned that the big six have more money than ever, and the gap is so huge it is impossible for any other club to compete with them, financially at least.

And this is an important point: other than Villa and Newcastle, the other clubs are not trying to compete with the big six.

Clubs like Brentford and Brighton have shown that smart models are just as effective as fat wallets.

They sign the potential stars of the future, nurture them and then sell them to the big six.

Football's ecosystem recycles the big-six money through the transfer market.

But it is a precarious business for these other clubs.

"The smaller clubs have to get it right on a more regular basis than the bigger clubs," Maguire said.

"The substantial six can afford to make signings which are Â£60m and Â£70m, who turn out to be relative flops, and still have those players on high wages for several years.".

And this is perhaps the key point about the vast finances of the massive six.

In a recent development, the commercial power of the significant six does not guarantee success. After all, United sit in the relegation zone.

Yet Mauricio Pochettino, their new manager, may well get the chance to revamp the squad despite the club spending Â£945m on players in the past five years.

In a recent development, the richest clubs can try to spend their way out of trouble. Again and again.

But the rest of the league are only a couple of bad transfer windows from catastrophe.

And that is the real gap between the substantial six and the rest.
